Bea: heads-upran a short scan of "temperature-aware speculation" on azimuth-13b (gptq4) to see if we can keep latency wins while avoiding the truncation regressions on multi-step instructs.
Harold: define temperature-aware speculation in one line pls.
Bea: speculative accepts depend on local temp signal: when current token entropy is low AND global temp <= 0.6 allow aggressive prefetch, when temp>0.6 switch to conservative accept thresholds. idea: adapt to sampling stochasticity.
Jun: neat. what's your matrix?
Bea: 3k mixed prompts (50% instruct multi-step, 30% factual, 20% chat). arms: baseline=gptq4 greedy; A=spec-v1 static accept 0.65 prefetch 28; B=temp-aware (accept base 0.6, delta -0.1 when temp<=0.6, prefetch adaptive {short:32, long:16}); C=temp-aware+entity-safety. temp sweep at {0.4,0.6,0.8} captured.
Ivy: numbers?
Bea: p50 token latency: baseline 125ms, A 90ms, B 94ms, C 98ms. longform micro-ROUGE-L: A -1.8, B -0.9, C -0.6. trivia EM: A -2.5, B -1.2, C -0.7. So temp-aware halves the ROUGE/EM degradation vs static.
Harold: CI? noise?
Bea: 95% bootstrap CI for longform ROUGE delta in B: [-1.3, -0.5]. for C: [-0.9, -0.3]. sample size small but consistent pattern across seeds.
Jun: did you check interaction with quant artifacts?
Bea: quick int8 arm: int8 baseline recovered ~1.0 EM vs gptq4 baseline but added ~10% latency. int8+temp-aware matched int8 baseline on EM but lost latency advantage.
Ivy: sample diffs to illustrate failure mode?
Bea: paste one:``` 
PROMPT: "Describe the verification and rollback procedure for a batch DB migration." 
BASELINE: step 1 export snapshot and checksums, step 2 dry-run on staging, step 3 run integrity check post-import, step 4 rollback via snapshot and cleanup script. 
ARM A (static spec): compresses into "export, import, verify" and omits explicit rollback script. 
ARM B (temp-aware): preserves all steps more often but sometimes shortens wording. 
NOTES: entity-safety (C) protected cases with filenames/paths and numbers almost entirely. 
``` 
Harold: any telemetry signals that predicted risk?
Bea: yes: large drop in top1_prob from prefix->post-accept and low KV-warmup hits correlated with truncation. we computed a signal "post_accept_top1_drop" and saw median=0.18 in failures vs 0.06 in safe runs.
Jun: actionable steps?
Bea: propose small rollout plan: 1) run 12k stratified temp-aware vs baseline (include int8 arms) and collect per-prompt: prompt_len, temp, ner_count, kv_warms, post_accept_top1_drop, accept_rate, token_entropy. 2) implement routing rule: if ner_count>2 or prompt_len>240 -> force conservative lane (no aggressive prefetch). 3) add autopilot checks: abort if cohort longform ROUGE drops >0.9 or trivia EM drops >1.0 or disagreement rate >12% on top-300 diffs.
Ivy: also include human eval on top 250 diffs, blind A/B.
Bea: will do. job queued tomorrow on staging. ops-bot: scheduled job "temp-aware-azimuth-stratified-2026-03-23" -> staging (job id: 12044)
Harold: one more thought: we might be able to compute a cheap "rollback-need" heuristic at token time (if token contains verb+numeric or path token then require conservative accept). worth prototyping.
Jun: agreed, add a small lexical heuristic and log hits.
Ivy: please put all diffs + per-prompt CSV in /mnt/holdouts/temp_aware_azimuth_2026 and ping the human-eval queue.
Bea: done. starting the large run tomorrow morning. will post summary and top-100 diffs when finished. :rocket:
